assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: No nested OpenCode session is allowed; csm-build owns instruction-led execution in the current agent context and returns typed results to csm-orchestrate.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: T001 must make full skill ownership coverage and the csm-build-owned instruction-execution handoff explicit before registry implementation.
Route-wide handler preflight must precede approval, idempotency, progress, cursor, and dispatch-intent mutation.
Capability, contract, handler, configuration, receipt/evidence schema, and artifact digests must be distinct and bound through replay.
Complete child terminal responses, side-effect class, attempt identity, and reconciliation state must be durable.
Final review must be independent in provenance and context, not merely assigned a different label or function.
Root and bootstrap payload changes, external caller migration, and zero-launch checks must be synchronized.

design.controlPlane: Keep orchestrate(), phase compiler, requirement ledger, approvals, evidence gates, adversarial review, remediation graph, cursor/store, receipts, and progress as authorities.
design.executionPlane: Add a versioned SkillExecutor registry separate from capabilities.json. Direct handlers resolve exact descriptors; instruction-led routes use an explicit csm-build-owned typed handoff descriptor pinned by contract, result, and configuration digests.
design.coverage: T001 produces a complete matrix. Procedural skills use direct handlers; instruction-led skills are executed by csm-build in the current agent context and return through a typed handoff. Missing handoff is deterministically BLOCKED and remains incomplete.
design.preflight: Compile all selected route nodes, resolve every handler and digest without mutation, then validate inputs and approval eligibility; only after success reserve idempotency, persist cursor/progress, consume approval, and create dispatch intent.
design.resultBoundary: Handlers return normalized child results, but the control plane validates owner/run/attempt identity, receipt/evidence/artifact schema, exact requirement signal entailment, declared outputs, size, and effect/failure class.
design.recovery: Persist complete per-attempt child terminal results and dispatch state. Handler timeout/cancellation/crash after dispatch becomes UNKNOWN until reconciliation; read-only retry may be policy-allowed, side-effecting retry is blocked until resolved.
design.reviewBoundary: Separate local gate calculation, adversarial phase review, and mandatory final review. Final review receives frozen requirements/evidence without producer rationale and has distinct reviewer identity, approval, digest, receipt, artifact, and durable record.
design.migration: Remove the default OpenCode CLI host after replacement coverage exists. Any external caller must receive an explicit executor-required migration path; no hidden compatibility fallback remains.
design.rollback: Keep the control-plane contract stable where possible. If a handler or registry migration fails, leave that route BLOCKED and restore only the executor selection boundary, never weaken evidence or approval gates.

executionGraph.integrationOwner: Primary build agent owns control-plane parity, registry integration, digest/recovery authority, packaging, migration, and final verification.

knownGaps: The external createCliHost caller is outside the checkout until discovered or supplied.
csm-build-owned instruction execution requires a current-context handoff at dispatch time.
Browser/network side effects require per-handler policy and may remain blocked without an approved adapter.
No test can prove arbitrary external effects exactly once; reconciliation is the required guarantee.

risks: The csm-build-owned handoff may be absent or return an invalid result at dispatch time.
Direct handlers may retain hidden subprocess/filesystem/network/browser effects.
Digest domains may drift across long-running executions.
Final review may be relabeled rather than genuinely independent.
Crash-after-effect ambiguity may be mistaken for ordinary failure.
External callers may depend on the old OpenCode host.
mitigations: Make T001 a hard coverage/feasibility gate and block rather than silently narrow scope.
Inventory and isolate every handler's effects and cancellation.
Persist and validate all digest domains at every authority boundary.
Require frozen context, distinct provenance, approval, and reviewer-owned terminal records.
Persist intent and complete child terminal results; reconcile UNKNOWN before side-effect retry.
Search and test migration callers before removing the old path.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Rollback only the executor-plane and packaging commit boundary while preserving existing control-plane evidence/approval/recovery authorities. Restore an explicit host-required BLOCKED boundary rather than restoring an implicit OpenCode default.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: If a route cannot be made callable safely, leave it BLOCKED with a recorded reason and keep the plan incomplete. If a durable record is ambiguous, stop for reconciliation. If the final review is unavailable, return REQUIRES_REVIEW and do not emit VERIFIED.
